This is a weak but persistent effect (about −0.08 pp, ~2σ).\n- Seeds 3–12 have now driven about 10 decisions, so the final candidates need fresh seeds 13–22.\n\n**Keep rule (H4).** A recipe whose true mean is 0.7526 passes the 3-seed bar only about 42% of the time; at 0.7545 it passes about 77% of the time. Keeps should require a held-out mean of about 0.7545. E027 is recorded as kept in breach of its own rule (held-out 0.7526 < 0.7535). H4.3.2 now targets whichever recipe is submitted.\n\n**Status fixes:**\n- **Refuted:** H1.6.1 (E029) and H1.3.7 (E030). E030 shows the airbench Lookahead schedule is a local optimum on both sides.\n- **H1.6:** inconclusive. One null result is not enough to close it.\n- **H1.3:** rewritten. I dropped the per-seed pairing argument and the stale \"less frequent resets\" candidate. BatchNorm-stat recompute (H1.3.6) goes up to 0.4, because airbench averages BatchNorm buffers along with the weights and a paper measured +0.48 pp from recomputing them on CIFAR-100. I lowered plain EMA (H1.3.5).\n- **H4.1.2 / H4.2.4:** H4.1.2 is now inconclusive (E016 and E017 broke its bound); H4.2.4 is supported.\n- **H4.2:** pooled E016 and E017 as one 9.5-epoch point. The epoch dial is about 0.37 pp per epoch, with an interval.\n- **H2.3:** I wrote the E011, E018 and E024 refutes into its statement. New items can't be given a refuted status, so I added no retroactive children.\n- **H1:** sourced the 59.3 s baseline to the organizer's ResNet9 run (from forks of the competition repo) and updated the tip to E027.\n\n**Muon and batch size downgraded.** H1.2 drops to 0.3, H1.2.1 is now inconclusive and H5 drops to 0.2. E006 changed Muon, batch size and the RNG stream at once, and an outside CIFAR-100 port found \"Muon lost to SGD at every size\". The direct ablation, H1.2.2, is now a priority. Search also says the reference Muon uses 3 Newton-Schulz steps and renormalises filters every step, which feeds into H1.2.3 and H1.5.4. H5.1.2 (a smaller batch) gets search support.\n\n**H1.5 softened.** Per the review, the earlier \"scalars are flat\" conclusions (label smoothing, Muon learning rate, LR floor) are now recorded as \"not detected at 3-seed power\". The weight-decay optimum is unresolved.\n\n**H3 and H3.2 reopened.** They now aim to cut about 0.05 s of fixed cost: trial 0's prepare takes 0.21 s against 0.06 s for the others. That is now about the size of the levers being pursued.\n\n**Committee counterexamples:**\n- E028 is explained by the new memory-bandwidth mechanism under H6.\n- E030 is explained by H1.3.7's refutation.\n- E024 is covered by H6.2 (off-grid tile sizes).\n- E018 and E026 are folded into H2.3.\n- E025's time miss came from forecasting against the wrong base, not from a missing mechanism."}

updates.statement: The number of epochs needed to reach 75% (sample efficiency) sets most of the wall time. Backbone, optimizer and regularization choices that cut epochs-to-target are the main lever. Together with resizing, compile and averaging they give about 10x over the organizer's 40-epoch ResNet9 baseline (59.30 s on an A100 80GB PCIe, from forks of the competition repo; not run in this loop) → 5.88 s at the E027 tip.
updates.reason: Review: the 59.3 s figure was unsourced and the tip was stale. Search sourced the baseline (organizer ResNet9, 59.30 s on A100 PCIe). Tip updated to E027.

E006 changed three things at once: Muon, batch 1024→2000 and an RNG re-draw. Its +0.66 pp is about 1.5–2σ under the later noise model. External evidence goes the other way: futurebiohackers' CIFAR-100 airbench port found that 'Muon lost to SGD at every size'. The committee votes supported, but nothing has tested it since E006. The decisive test is H1.2.2.
E006 never compared against SGD tuned at batch 2000, so it cannot support a Muon-vs-SGD-at-equal-batch claim. Its confounds are batch size and RNG re-draw.

updates.statement: On the current tip (E027, or its freeze successor), replace Muon on the conv filters with Nesterov SGD (lr and wd scaled for batch 2000, everything else unchanged). Prediction: the held-out seeds 3–12 mean drops by at least 0.3 pp and time falls by about 3% (the Muon NS overhead measured in E006). If the loss is under 0.15 pp, E006's gain came from batch size or the RNG re-draw, and dropping Muon is about 3% free time.
updates.reason: Rebased onto the current tip. Priority raised: external evidence (futurebiohackers: Muon lost to SGD on CIFAR-100) and the review both say the E006 attribution is untested. Confidence that Muon is worth ≥0.3 pp lowered from 0.5 to 0.4.

updates.statement: Cutting Muon per-step cost on the tip cuts mean time by at least 1.5% and keeps the held-out mean within 0.15 pp. The means: reduce Newton-Schulz iterations to 3 (airbench94_muon and Hiverge both use 3; check how many the port uses). If the filters are renormalized every step, renormalize progressively less often (Hiverge: every 2 steps rising to every 17).
updates.reason: Search: the reference Muon uses 3 NS steps and per-step filter renormalization, and Hiverge thins renormalization. Rebased onto the tip with a held-out criterion. The saving is capped by E006's ~3.8% total Muon overhead.

updates.statement: In short CIFAR-100 runs, end-of-run averaging is a first-order lever. Lookahead/EMA gave +0.97 pp at E005, about 2.5–3σ against an unpaired 3-seed SE. Seeds do not pair across recipes (H4.1c), so per-seed gains are not consistency evidence, and the effect's current size on the tip is unmeasured. The airbench schedule is a local optimum on both sides. A harder or earlier pull hurt (E025: alpha exponent 2, −0.27 pp held-out). Longer free runs between resets also hurt (E030: every 10 steps, −0.24 pp held-out). With averaging on, the final-LR floor does not matter (E009, C0021). The reset itself probably carries part of the gain (Switch-EMA, C0024). Untested candidates: recomputing BN stats for the averaged weights (Lookahead lerps BN buffers too, so the final stats are a mixture), plain EMA without resets, and dropping label smoothing late.
updates.reason: Review: removed the per-seed pairing argument, removed 'less frequent resets' (refuted by E030), and recorded E025/E030 as local-optimum evidence (each ~2.3σ, so tuning is not formally closed). Search: airbench96_faster lerps every float in state_dict, including BN running stats.
E030 shows the reset cadence matters: longer free runs hurt. This, together with C0024 (Switch-EMA beats plain EMA), makes it less likely that plain EMA beats Lookahead.

updates.statement: On the current tip (E027, or the freeze successor if kept), recompute BN running statistics for the final averaged weights: one 32 px train-mode forward over at most 5k training images, with BN momentum set so the stats reflect only those batches, inside timed train. Prediction: the held-out seeds 3–12 mean rises by at least 0.2 pp, at a cost under 0.1 s. Airbench's Lookahead lerps BN buffers along with the weights, so the final running stats are a mixture over different fast weights, and BN momentum 0.6 makes them noisy.
updates.reason: Search: arXiv 2411.18704 measured +0.48 pp on CIFAR-100/ResNet-18 from a BN recompute after EMA. airbench96_faster averages the BN buffers rather than recomputing them. The committee votes refuted (3), which conflicts with this literature, so it needs a decisive, cheap test. Rebased onto the current tip.

E030: Lookahead every 10 steps with rescaled alpha gave held-out 0.7502 vs E027's 0.7526 (−0.24 pp, ~2.4σ). The prediction was +0.15 pp. Seeds 0–2 also fell (0.7492). This explains committee counterexample E030: resetting the fast weights less often lets them drift further from the average in the high-LR phase.

Committee votes refuted 3 / unknown 1. E013 found no detectable LS effect between 0.2 and 0.3 at 3-seed power, so a late LS change is unlikely to move ≥0.15 pp. It stays open only as a cheap, time-neutral test.

updates.statement: The optimizer and regularization settings copied from CIFAR-10 airbench may not be optimal for short CIFAR-100 runs. The only effect measured on held-out seeds is wd ×0.5 (E016 vs E010/E012: +0.24 pp, ~2σ). Its optimum is unresolved: E022's ×0.25 on the SGD groups was −0.24 pp vs E017 but only −0.11 pp vs E016. The LS 0.2 vs 0.3 (E013), Muon lr ×1.5 (E014) and LR-floor (E009) results are 'not detected at 3-seed power', not 'flat': those tests could not resolve 0.2–0.3 pp. Untested on held-out: LS 0.1, Muon lr ×2, and a shrinking filter-norm target instead of wd (Hiverge).
updates.reason: Review: the 'scalars are flat' conclusions rest on 3-seed differences of 0.04–0.09 pp, below what those tests can resolve. The committee votes refuted (3), and the evidence for flatness is weak in both directions. Confidence lowered slightly; status left open.
Kept inconclusive. E016's gain is confounded with the E015 cudagraph rebuild, and E015 was never run on held-out seeds. On held-out, E016 is +0.24 pp over E010/E012 (~2σ): weak support only.

updates.statement: E016's gain came from the SGD groups, not the Muon filters. Starting from the tip, restoring the original wd on the Muon conv filters only keeps the held-out mean within 0.15 pp. First check in the code whether the port renormalizes filters every step as airbench94_muon does (p.data.mul_(len(p)**0.5 / p.norm())). If it does, filter wd is inert and this is settled by reading the code, with no run needed.
updates.reason: Search confirmed that the reference renormalizes filters every step, which makes filter wd inert. Criterion changed to held-out. Low priority per the review.
The review asks for a held-out retest, since E013 was underpowered. The committee all expect refuted; Hiverge uses LS 0.09 on CIFAR-10. Kept open as one of the two cheapest scalar retests.
The held-out E016 vs E010/E012 difference (+0.24 pp, ~2σ) suggests that restoring wd ×1 lowers the mean by about 0.2 pp, but the committee all vote refuted. Low priority per the review.

Its only test, H1.6.1 (E029: warm-up halved, −0.05 pp held-out), found no effect. Hiverge uses no warm-up at all, which is consistent with a flat dial. The committee votes refuted (3). Not closed on one null result within noise; peak and EMA-start re-timing relative to the resolution phases are untested.
E029: halving the warm-up gave held-out 0.7521 vs 0.7526 (−0.05 pp). The prediction was ≥+0.2 pp. Seeds 0–2 were 0.7526.

updates.statement: At a fixed epoch count, the cost per epoch (systems overhead plus FLOPs and memory traffic per sample) is a large lever. Levers found so far: compile/fusion (−14%, E004), progressive resizing (−22%, E007; −2.9%, E026) and backward truncation of the high-resolution stem late in training (−8.8% at no held-out cost, E028). Launch overhead is exhausted (E015, E017).
updates.reason: Records E028 (backward truncation) as a third proven category of per-epoch cost cut, and notes that launch overhead is exhausted.

updates.statement: Progressive resizing is a near-linear time dial for tile-friendly sizes (about 0.51/0.71/0.89 s per epoch at 24/28/32 px, E012). Accuracy is carried by the 28 and 32 px phases. E007's 24/28/32 at 40/30/30 is cheap, and so is a short early 20 px phase (E026: −0.15 pp held-out, ~1.5σ, unresolved). Refuted variants: E018 (drop the 28 px phase: −0.68 pp held-out, ~0.8 s/pp), E011 (20 px start plus a 20% 32 px tail: −0.97 pp on 3 seeds, confounded) and E024 (26 px middle phase: −0.25 pp for −2%, ~0.5 s/pp, off-grid tiles; see H6.2). These record the Lvl3 refutes that were logged against this Lvl2. Candidate mechanisms: (a) low resolution during the peak-LR window; (b) a FixRes object-scale and BN-statistics shift at the final jump; (c) too little full-resolution fine-tuning while LR decays and averaging forms (C0011). The attribution of E011's loss to the 32 px tail comes from subtracting a 3-seed number from a held-out number and is unproven (H2.3.7 is the control).
updates.reason: Bookkeeping (review): the E011/E018/E024 refutes belong to unlisted children. They are now written into the statement so the Lvl2's 'supported' status reflects the dial being real, not those variants. Added the caveat about attributing E011's loss to the tail.
The committee unanimously expects refuted, and the LS dial showed no detectable effect at 0.2–0.3 (E013). Lowered further.
The committee votes refuted (3). The proxy forward cost plus the memory-bound large-map work (E028) make selective backprop unattractive at this scale.

E028 suggests that group-1 work on the 31×31 maps costs more than its MAC share (~27% of a 32 px step for the group-1 backward). Dropping a group-1 conv may therefore save more time than its FLOPs suggest. Never run; the review flags it.

updates.statement: Truncating the backward pass at the high-resolution stem late in training cuts per-step cost far more than its FLOP share, at little accuracy cost. The whitening layer and group 1 change little late in training, and their backward on the largest maps is memory-bound. E028 froze group 1 and the whitening bias for the last 25% of steps and saved ~9.5 ms per 32 px step (~27%). Air bench (whitening bias trained for 3 epochs only, 'without reducing accuracy'), Hiverge (whitening bias trained for the first 20% of steps) and FreezeOut (~20% saving with no loss on ResNets/WRNs, including CIFAR-100) are published precedents. Open extensions: freeze earlier, freeze the whitening bias earlier, switch frozen BN to eval mode or fold it into the conv, and stagger the freezes.
updates.reason: E028: −8.8% time and −0.01 pp held-out vs E027. Search found three independent precedents. Accuracy neutrality rests on one 10-seed comparison (SE ~0.11 pp), so confidence is moderate.

E028: −8.8% time (prediction ≥4%) and held-out 0.7525 vs E027's 0.7526 (prediction ≤0.2 pp loss). Discarded only because seeds 0–2 (0.7517) lost the lottery at a population mean at the bar. Caveats: (1) one 10-seed comparison; (2) the LR re-anneal and the truncation are confounded; (3) the idea text says 'E023 tip'. The notebook's per-step arithmetic (0.51 s / 55 frozen steps ≈ 9.3 ms ≈ 27% of a 35.6 ms 32 px step) fits the E027 base with 219 steps, but verify the step count in commit fcacfc6. If the base was E023, the held-out cost would be −0.31 pp vs E023's 0.7556 and the accuracy half would fail.

updates.statement: Fixed, epoch-independent cost inside timed prepare+train is about 1–2% of a ~5.4–5.9 s run, now comparable to the levers being pursued (E026 −0.18 s, E027 −0.14 s), and part of it is removable. Sources: prepare (0.21 s on trial 0 vs 0.06 s on trials 1–2, E004), the first-epoch warm-up in trial 0 (~60 ms, E012), and whitening init.
updates.reason: Re-opened with a revised threshold. The >5% claim was refuted (E012), but the run has shrunk from ~9 s to ~5.9 s. The review notes that trial 0's extra ~0.15 s in prepare suggests a one-time warm-up leaking into timed code, and that build may legally warm it up.

updates.statement: prepare() (dataset to GPU, normalization, whitening init) averages about 0.1 s per trial (0.21 s on trial 0, 0.06 s after) and can be cut by at least 0.05 s on the mean. The ways: uint8 transfer with normalization on the GPU, whitening from a small patch subset, and warming up in build (on synthetic data) whatever makes trial 0 slower.
updates.reason: Re-opened per the review with an absolute target matched to current lever sizes. The original 5% threshold was refuted.

updates.statement: Moving the data as uint8 with GPU normalization, computing the whitening from at most 5k images, and warming the first-call kernels and allocations used by prepare in build (synthetic tensors only) cuts the 3-trial mean prepare+train time by at least 0.05 s. The held-out mean stays within 0.1 pp; the whitening estimate changes, so the RNG trajectory re-draws.
updates.reason: Revived with the review's 0.05 s target. Cheap, and orthogonal to the accuracy-margin problem.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the accuracy margin: the best time comes from sitting just above the 0.753 3-seed bar while still holding ≥0.75 over 40 seeds. The seeds 0–2 mean is an unbiased but noisy estimate of the population mean (offset RMS ~0.20 pp over 15 recipes). A recipe at population mean m therefore passes the local bar with probability about Φ((m−0.753)/0.2): ~42% at 0.7526 (E027/E028) and ~77% at 0.7545. Keeps should be gated on a held-out mean of at least ~0.7545, not on the bar. E027 was kept against its own pre-registered rule (held-out 0.7526 < 0.7535), so the tip is feasible only by luck.
updates.reason: Review: E027 was kept in breach of its rule, and E028 lost the same coin flip at an equal population mean. Offset RMS recomputed from the 15 recipes with held-out data (E012, E016–E030): RMS ≈0.20 pp, mean ≈0. That is close to pure sampling noise (expected ~0.16 pp) and smaller than the 0.3–0.4 pp quoted earlier.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise has three parts. (a) Rebuild noise: no-cudagraph artifacts are bit-identical per seed, and max-autotune/cudagraph rebuilds move the 3-seed mean only about ±0.03 pp (E019). (b) Seed and test-set noise: per-seed std is 0.15–0.35 pp (organizer: 0.25 pp over 50 trials). (c) Trajectory re-draw: any change to the math or to random-number use re-draws every seed, so per-seed differences across recipes carry little information (E025: seeds 0–2 +0.19 pp, held-out −0.27 pp). Over 15 recipes the seeds 0–2 vs seeds 3–12 offset has mean ≈0 and RMS ≈0.20 pp. Only E016 (+0.43) and E017 (−0.40) exceed 0.3 pp, so the pure-sampling model (expected ~0.16 pp) fits with a small excess. There is a weak persistent seed component: seed 1 is the lowest of seeds 0–2 in about 10 of 18 recipes (seed-1 residual mean about −0.08 pp, ~2σ). Difference of two 10-seed means: SE ≈0.10 pp. Decisions need at least 2–2.5σ. Seeds 3–12 have now driven about 10 keep/discard decisions, so they carry their own winner's curse; the final candidates need fresh seeds 13–22.
updates.reason: Review: noted the persistent seed-1 effect and the reuse of held-out seeds. Recomputed the offset distribution from all held-out runs: the 0.3–0.4 pp figure was driven by E016/E017, and the overall RMS is ~0.20 pp.

The prediction (held-out within 0.3 pp of seeds 0–2) held for E010/E012 (−0.08) and for 13 of the 15 recipes since, but E016 (+0.43) and E017 (−0.40) broke it. The rule holds about 87% of the time, not reliably.

updates.statement: Near the tip, true epochs are a smooth dial. Pooling E016 and E017 as the 9.5-epoch point (0.7570, 20 seeds), the held-out points are 9.5: 0.7570, 9.0: 0.7556, 8.5: 0.7533, a slope of about 0.37 pp per epoch (interval roughly 0.25–0.5). The three points span two crop implementations. Each true epoch costs about 0.68 s, so the dial trades about 1.5–2.7 s/pp. E028's freeze (≥5 s/pp; −0.52 s for −0.01 pp) is the only lever clearly better than the dial. E018 (~0.8), E024 (~0.5) and E021 (~1.0 s/pp) are clearly worse. E026 (~1.2 s/pp, CI 0.7–3.6) cannot be separated from the dial. Rank dials only when the intervals separate.
updates.reason: Review: pooled E016/E017 as the 9.5-epoch anchor and gave the slope with an interval. Added E028 as the one lever that beats the dial.

E020 (−1.0 ep: −0.44 pp held-out, −10.5%), E023 (−0.5 ep: −0.21 pp held-out, −5.3%, seeds 0–2 0.7538 ≥0.7545? no, 0.7538 is just below but held-out 0.7556 clears it) and E027 (−0.25 ep: −0.15 pp, −2.3%) all match the 0.1–0.45 pp per 0.5 epoch and ~5% time prediction. Consistent across three points.

updates.statement: Local SXM4 results transfer to the PCIe judge only partly. Kernel reselection on the judge's own build shifts the mean only slightly (about ±0.03 pp, E019), so the accuracy risk comes from seed noise and from the population mean sitting near the bar. A held-out mean of at least about 0.753 gives enough headroom over the 40-seed bar of 0.75. Caveat on time ranking: E028 shows part of the step is memory-bandwidth-bound, not compute-bound. The PCIe card's lower power cap and clocks may shift the relative value of compute-bound levers (resizing, epochs) and bandwidth-bound ones (backward truncation). This cannot be tested locally; record which kept levers are of which kind once profiling exists.
updates.reason: Review: the GPU-bound transfer assumption needs a bandwidth caveat after E028.

updates.statement: The final candidate's margin is real. Run offline on fresh seeds 13–22, the recipe to be submitted (the freeze successor, or E027) gives a mean within 0.15 pp of its seeds 3–12 mean, and the pooled 20-seed mean is at least 0.753 (SE about 0.05 pp).
updates.reason: E027's held-out mean (0.7526) is already below 0.753, so the old E026-specific form is moot. Re-targeted at the final candidate. The committee leans refuted (2) because of the winner's curse on reused seeds 3–12.

updates.statement: At a fixed number of data passes, the optimizer step count (batch size) sets accuracy independently of the epoch count. Muon's critical batch may be smaller than AdamW's (arXiv 2507.01598), and Hiverge's record uses batch 1536 under Muon, which suggests batch 2000 may be above the optimum for a ~220-step run. E006's +0.66 pp is not evidence for this: it confounded Muon, batch 1024→2000 and an RNG re-draw.
updates.reason: Review: stop citing E006 as evidence for H5's mechanism. Search: the smaller-critical-batch result and Hiverge's 1536 point the other way from the original 'large critical batch' framing. Nothing has been tested.

Search (Hiverge batch 1536; Muon has a smaller critical batch, arXiv 2507.01598) supports testing a smaller batch first. The committee all vote refuted, so it needs a decisive held-out test, preferably rebased onto the current tip.

updates.statement: The per-pixel cost of the step is not uniform, so a systems or architecture lever worth at least 5% remains at near-identical math. Two regimes: (a) small maps (7×7, 3×3, off-grid 25/12/6) under-use the tensor cores (E021, E024); (b) large maps (group 1 and the whitening output at 31×31) are dominated by memory-bandwidth-bound BN/GELU/pool forward and backward (E028: removing group-1 backward saved ~27% of a 32 px step for ~20% of conv MACs). E011's '95% pixel-proportional' fit cannot separate compute from memory traffic, because both scale with pixels.
updates.reason: Explains committee counterexample E028 (time far below every range). The old framing (small maps, tensor cores only) missed bandwidth-bound work on the large maps. The profiling hypotheses (H2.2.4, H6.1.1, H6.2.1) have been open for ~13 experiments and should run now.

new.statement: On the E027 tip, apply E028's freeze (group 1 + whitening bias frozen for the last 25% of steps, group-1 LR annealed to 0 by then) and add 0.5 true epoch (8.75 → 9.25 true epochs, ~231 steps at batch 2000; LR, EMA and resolution schedules stretched). Prediction: mean time ≤5.75 s (below E027's 5.88 s) and a held-out seeds 3–12 mean of at least 0.7540. The keep gate is held-out ≥0.7545 plus seeds 0–2 ≥0.753.

If the port trains the whitening bias for the whole run, stopping its gradient after 20% of steps (Hiverge; airbench96 uses 3 of 45 epochs) removes the input-gradient of group 1's first conv and the BN/GELU backward feeding it on the 31×31 maps for the remaining steps. Prediction on the tip (or the freeze successor): mean time cut by at least 2%, with no more than 0.1 pp loss in the held-out mean. If the port already stops it early, this is settled by reading the code.

Freeze dose: on the N_freeze_epochs recipe, moving the group-1 freeze start from 75% to 60% of steps (group-1 LR annealed to 0 by 60%) cuts mean time by at least 3% more and loses no more than 0.15 pp of the held-out mean. This would beat the epoch dial (~1.5–2.7 s/pp).

During the frozen phase, switching group-1 BN to eval mode (running stats set from a batch-stat pass at the freeze point, then folded into the conv weights) removes the per-step BN statistics passes on the 31×31 maps. Prediction: mean time cut by at least 2% beyond E028's train-mode-BN freeze, with no more than 0.15 pp held-out loss.

E028's accuracy neutrality depends on re-annealing the group-1 LR to 0 before the freeze. An abrupt freeze at 75% with the global LR schedule kept for group 1 until then loses at least 0.15 pp of the held-out mean compared with E028's annealed freeze, at equal time.

On the largest maps (whitening output and group 1 at 31×31), the BN, GELU and pooling forward and backward kernels are memory-bandwidth-bound and take a larger share of step time than their FLOPs. Levers that cut large-map activation traffic (backward truncation, fewer group-1 layers, BN folding when frozen) therefore save more than their MAC share. This explains E028's ~27% per-step saving for ~20% of conv MACs.

A torch.profiler trace of one 32 px train step of the tip shows non-GEMM kernels (BN, GELU, pool, elementwise; forward plus backward) taking at least 30% of GPU time, and group 1 plus the whitening layer (forward plus backward) taking at least 35% of the step, more than group 1's ~20% share of conv MACs.

structured_output.summary:
I made 37 updates to the hypothesis tree and added 7 new hypotheses. The biggest shift: E028's FreezeOut-style freeze is now the leading lever, and the open questions are about accuracy margin rather than speed.

**FreezeOut (E028) is now supported.** H2.6 and H2.6.1 are marked supported (confidence about 0.6). E028 cut time 8.8% and lost only 0.01 pp on the held-out seeds 3–12. It was discarded only because seeds 0–2 lost what is close to a coin flip at a population mean sitting at the bar. Two caveats:
- **Base needs checking.** The idea text says the run was built on E023, while the notebook treats E027 as the base. The per-step arithmetic fits E027 (219 steps). If the base was really E023, the held-out cost would be −0.31 pp, not −0.01. Check commit fcacfc6 before relying on this.
- **Confound.** The learning-rate re-anneal and the backward truncation changed together, so it isn't known which one keeps accuracy flat.

New children of H2.6:
- **Next run:** the freeze plus 0.5 epoch on the E027 tip. Predicted time ≤5.75 s and held-out mean ≥0.7540.
- **Whitening bias:** stop its gradient early, as airbench and Hiverge do.
- **Earlier freeze:** start at 60% of steps instead of 75%.
- **Frozen BatchNorm:** switch it to eval mode and fold it into the conv.
- **Confound test:** freeze abruptly without the learning-rate re-anneal.

**H6 reframed.** E028 also explains a committee counterexample. Removing group 1's backward saved about 27% of a 32 px step, although group 1 is only about 20% of conv MACs. So the step has two inefficient regimes:
- small maps that underuse the tensor cores (E021, E024);
- large 31×31 maps where BatchNorm/GELU work is limited by memory bandwidth.

I added that second regime as a new mechanism, with a profiler prediction under it. The profiling hypotheses have been open for about 13 experiments and should run now.

**Noise model corrected.** I recomputed the gap between the seeds 0–2 mean and the held-out mean across all 15 recipes that have held-out runs. It averages about 0 with an RMS of about 0.20 pp, not the 0.3–0.4 pp quoted earlier. That is close to pure sampling noise; only E016 and E017 were outliers. Two other notes went into H4.1:
- Seed 1 is the lowest of seeds 0–2 in 10 of 18 recipes. This is a weak but persistent effect (about −0.08 pp, ~2σ).
